newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank assurances fail to boost market.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank assurances fail to boost market.

text.p: Assurances by the Bank of Thailand on Tuesday that finance and securities firms were financially sound did not halt the bourse's downward spiral, and analysts expect the slide to continue.

The Bank of Thailand (BOT) said in a statement that it had reviewed finance and securities firms, some of which have been hit by rumours that they were in trouble, and found them to be in good credit standing.
"These companies have and will continue to operate normally under a close supervision of the Bank of Thailand," the BOT said in a statement.

Rumours that several brokerages had been hit by client defaults on margin loans triggered forced selling of financially weak investors' stocks recently, bringing the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index down to near three-year lows.

Under forced selling, investors must pay cash for stocks that they bought on margin if prices drop below 40 percent of the purchase value of the stocks. If investors cannot find the funds, they will be ordered by their brokers to sell the shares.

"The general public should refrain from reacting to unsubstantiated news or rumours which could inadvertently disrupt the operation of otherwise healthy financial institutions," the central bank said in its statement.
The BOT statement, and similar announcements by the SET and some finance firms, failed to boost the market, which closed again on Tuesday below the 1,000-point level.
The market finished down 4.29 points, or 0.43 percent, at 982.03 after falling as low as 975.51. The close was the lowest since September 30, 1993 when the index ended at 971.44.
"It's ugly. But there's still a way to go," an analyst said.
The bourse's recent decline was not only due to the rumours of possible problems with finance and securities firms, analysts said.

Other factors affecting the market include Thailand's slowdown in exports and gross domestic product growth and the political uncertainty ahead of a no-confidence debate against the government later this month.

"Interest rates are still near their recent historical highs, and the economy is still showing signs of slowing down," Todd Martin of SBC Warburg said. "Why should this be the bottom? We've probably got further to go."

The central bank also said it was ready to use its various mechanisms to ensure proper liquidity in the money market. The rumours about the health of finance firms also led to tighter liquidity in the money market this week.

It said the Financial Institutions Development Fund, a unit of the central bank set up to rescue troubled banks and finance companies, was prepared to participate more actively in the interbank market to ensure liquidity is allocated efficiently.

On Monday, the central bank injected up to 14 billion baht ($560 million) into the money market to ease tight liquidity. The injection helped the interbank rate ease to 12-12.5 percent late on Tuesday from 13.5-14.0 percent late on Monday.
